title: Wesleyan University (Wesleyan)
summary: Wesleyan University (Wesleyan) is a university in Middletown. This entry compiles College Scorecard figures and related sources; UniRepository is not affiliated with Wesleyan.

sections.heading: What Wesleyan is known for
paragraphs: Wesleyan University (Wesleyan) is a private nonprofit institution known for its selective undergraduate admissions, with an admission rate of approximately 16.5%. The university enrolls around 3,067 undergraduate students. While Wesleyan does not have programs in health or business fields, it is recognized for its commitment to a broad liberal arts education. As a private nonprofit college, Wesleyan emphasizes a diverse academic environment and a strong focus on undergraduate teaching.

sections.heading: Key strengths
paragraphs: Wesleyan University (Wesleyan) is a private nonprofit institution that offers a distinctive liberal arts education. Although it does not have programs in health fields and only a small portion of its offerings—approximately 1.36%—are in education, Wesleyan is recognized for its broad academic curriculum and commitment to undergraduate teaching. The university's private nonprofit status supports its focus on providing a diverse and rigorous educational experience.

sections.heading: Popular majors
paragraphs: Wesleyan University (Wesleyan) offers a variety of academic programs, with popular majors reflecting its liberal arts focus. sections.heading: Undergraduate admissions
paragraphs: Undergraduate admissions at Wesleyan University are highly selective, with an admission rate of approximately 16.49%. The university seeks students who demonstrate strong academic abilities and a commitment to intellectual growth. The average SAT score for admitted students is 1501, reflecting the competitive nature of the applicant pool. Wesleyan evaluates applications holistically, considering various aspects of each candidate's background and achievements.

sections.heading: How to read Wesleyan tuition
paragraphs: Wesleyan University (Wesleyan) charges a tuition fee of $70,342 for both in-state and out-of-state students. This uniform tuition rate applies regardless of residency status. The total cost of attendance, which includes tuition along with additional expenses such as room, board, and fees, amounts to $89,020. When evaluating the financial commitment required to attend Wesleyan, it is important to consider both the tuition and the overall cost of attendance to gain a comprehensive understanding of the expenses involved.

sections.heading: Financial aid
paragraphs: Wesleyan University (Wesleyan) provides financial aid to support students in managing the cost of attendance. Approximately 14.19% of students receive Pell Grants, which are federal subsidies aimed at assisting low-income students. Among those who complete their studies, the median debt incurred is $17,000, reflecting the typical borrowing amount upon graduation. Prospective students and families can use Wesleyan's net price calculator available on the university's official website to estimate personalized financial aid packages. Additional financial data and resources are accessible through the College Scorecard platform, which offers detailed insights into Wesleyan's cost and aid statistics.

paragraphs: Wesleyan University (Wesleyan) maintains a diverse student body with a gender distribution of approximately 47.83% men and 52.17% women.
